scams.name: Lakeside Pickpocketing
scams.description: Pickpockets operate around Lake Annecy, the Palais de l'Ile, and other popular tourist spots. They often work in pairs or groups, using distraction techniques while an accomplice rifles through bags and pockets. Crowded lakefront promenades during summer are particularly targeted.
scams.avoidance: Use a cross-body bag with zipped compartments. Keep valuables in front pockets or inside jacket pockets. Stay alert in crowded areas. Never leave bags on chairs or the ground in restaurants.
scams.location: Lake Annecy promenade, Palais de l'Ile, Old Town (Vieille Ville), popular markets

scams.name: Beach Belongings Theft
scams.description: Thieves patrol the beaches around Lake Annecy watching for swimmers who leave belongings unattended on the shore. They wait until targets are in the water or facing away, then quickly grab valuables and disappear. Summer months see increased incidents at popular swimming spots.
scams.avoidance: Never bring valuables to the beach. Leave jewelry and passports at your hotel. Use a waterproof pouch for essentials. Take turns swimming with companions so someone watches belongings.
scams.location: Plage d'Albigny, Plage des Marquisats, Plage de Talloires, all lakeside beaches

scams.name: Dual Menu Restaurant Scam
scams.description: Some restaurants in tourist areas maintain two sets of menus - one for locals with standard prices and another for tourists with inflated prices. Additionally, menus may lack prices entirely, only revealing exorbitant costs when the bill arrives. Hidden charges for bread, water, or cover fees may appear.
scams.avoidance: French law requires restaurants to display menus with prices outside. Ask for a menu with prices before ordering. Walk away from restaurants without posted prices. Verify the bill matches menu prices.
scams.location: Old Town restaurants near Palais de l'Ile, lakefront terraces, areas near major attractions

scams.name: Fake Petition and Charity Clipboard Scam
scams.description: Scammers approach tourists with clipboards asking them to sign petitions for supposed charitable causes. After signing, they demand donations of 10-20 euros. The clipboard distracts victims while accomplices pickpocket bags. The petitions feature photocopied logos from legitimate charities but are entirely fraudulent.
scams.avoidance: Never stop for anyone with a clipboard. Say 'Non merci' firmly and keep walking. Keep hands on your belongings if approached. Legitimate charities do not solicit on streets with petitions.
scams.location: Old Town pedestrian areas, near major attractions, market areas, lakefront promenade

scams.name: The Gold Ring Trick
scams.description: A scammer 'finds' a gold ring on the ground near a tourist and asks if they dropped it. When the tourist says no, the scammer offers to sell it as a 'lucky find' for a significant sum, claiming it is valuable gold. The ring is worthless metal. This scam, common in Paris, occasionally appears in smaller French tourist towns.
scams.avoidance: Never engage with anyone claiming to find valuables near you. Say 'Non' and walk away immediately. Do not touch or examine anything offered.
scams.location: Pedestrian areas, lakefront, near tourist attractions

scams.name: Friendship Bracelet Scam
scams.description: Scammers aggressively approach tourists and begin tying a 'friendship bracelet' onto their wrist without permission. Once the bracelet is tied, they demand payment, often 10-20 euros or more, becoming aggressive if refused. While attempting to remove the bracelet, accomplices may pickpocket the distracted victim.
scams.avoidance: Keep your hands in pockets or crossed when walking. Never let strangers touch your hands or wrists. Walk away immediately saying 'Non merci' firmly.
scams.location: Pedestrian zones, Old Town, near popular photo spots

scams.name: Rental Car Break-ins
scams.description: Thieves target rental cars which are easy to identify by license plates, lack of floor mats, and sterile interiors. They smash windows to steal luggage, electronics, and valuables, sometimes dropping rear seats to access trunks. Parking areas near trailheads and scenic viewpoints are frequently targeted.
scams.avoidance: Never leave any valuables visible in your car. Remove all items including charging cables. Use staffed parking lots when available. Consider sedan rentals with proper trunks rather than hatchbacks.
scams.location: Trailhead parking areas, scenic viewpoints around the lake, unstaffed parking lots, street parking

scams.name: Vacation Rental Fraud
scams.description: Scammers create fake vacation rental listings for properties in Annecy that either do not exist or belong to someone else. Victims pay deposits or full amounts via bank transfer only to arrive and find no accommodation. Some scammers create sophisticated fake booking websites mimicking legitimate platforms.
scams.avoidance: Only book through official platforms like Airbnb or Booking.com. Never pay via bank transfer or cryptocurrency. Read reviews carefully. Verify property addresses on Google Maps.
scams.location: Online - affects pre-trip booking for Annecy accommodations

scams.name: ATM Skimming and Distraction
scams.description: Criminals install skimming devices on ATMs to capture card data and PINs. Others pose as helpful locals at ATMs or ticket machines, offering assistance while memorizing PIN codes or switching cards. An international ring was busted in 2025 after stealing over 580,000 euros across Western Europe.
scams.avoidance: Use ATMs inside banks during business hours. Cover the keypad completely when entering PINs. Decline help from strangers at ATMs. Check card slots for loose attachments before inserting cards.
scams.location: Standalone ATMs, tourist area cash machines, train station ticket machines

scams.name: Distraction Theft by Groups
scams.description: Thieves work in organized groups using distraction techniques. One person creates a diversion - asking for directions, showing a map, dropping items, or staging an argument - while accomplices pickpocket the distracted tourist. They particularly target visitors taking photos or consulting phones and maps.
scams.avoidance: Be immediately suspicious if approached by strangers, especially in groups. Secure your belongings first if someone creates a scene. Keep your phone and wallet in front pockets or secured pouches. Travel with a companion who can watch your back.
scams.location: Old Town, lakefront, popular photo spots, market areas, near the canal

scams.name: Pickpocketing at Tourist Hotspots
scams.description: Pickpocketing is the most common crime affecting tourists in Avignon. Thieves operate in crowded areas around the Palace of the Popes, Pont d'Avignon, Place de l'Horloge, and train stations. They often work in teams with one person creating a distraction. During the Festival d'Avignon in July, incidents increase significantly.
scams.avoidance: Use a cross-body bag worn to the front with secure zippers, or a money belt worn discreetly under clothing. Never leave phones, wallets, or bags unattended. Be especially vigilant in crowds.
scams.location: Palace of the Popes, Place de l'Horloge, Pont d'Avignon, Avignon train stations, Les Halles market

scams.name: Petition Clipboard Scam
scams.description: Groups of scammers, often pretending to be deaf or representing charities, approach visitors asking 'Do you speak English?' followed by a request to sign a petition. The petition is typically in English (suspicious in France). While you hold the clipboard, an accomplice rifles through your pockets or bags. They may also demand a donation after signing.
scams.avoidance: Firmly say 'non merci' and walk away without engaging. Never hold a clipboard offered by strangers. Keep your hands free and bags secured when approached.
scams.location: Tourist areas around major monuments, Place de l'Horloge, near train stations

scams.name: Fake Police Officer Scam
scams.description: Fake police officers approach tourists, flashing bogus badges and demanding to see your passport and wallet to 'check for counterfeit bills.' While examining your wallet, they discreetly remove bills. Some pose as 'Tourist Police' to appear more legitimate.
scams.avoidance: Real French police will never ask to see your wallet on the street. Never hand over your passport or wallet. Inform them you will call the local police to verify their identity (dial 17). Walk toward a busy public area.
scams.location: Tourist areas, train stations, near hotels

scams.name: Taxi Overcharging
scams.description: Unofficial taxi drivers target tourists at the Avignon TGV station and airport, offering rides at inflated rates. Even official taxis may display night tariffs during daytime, claim the meter is broken, or take long routes to inflate fares.
scams.avoidance: Only use official taxis from designated taxi stands. Check that the meter shows the correct daytime tariff. Look for the official taxi sign on the roof. Use ride-hailing apps when possible.
scams.location: Avignon TGV station, Avignon Centre station, Avignon airport

scams.name: Festival d'Avignon Crowd Scams
scams.description: During the annual Festival d'Avignon each July, the city swells with hundreds of thousands of visitors. This creates ideal conditions for pickpockets who take advantage of distracted crowds watching street performances, queuing for shows, or navigating packed streets. Street vendors also inflate prices significantly.
scams.avoidance: Be extra vigilant during the festival period (early to late July). Keep valuables in front cross-body bags or hidden money belts. Avoid carrying large amounts of cash. Be especially careful when watching street performances.
scams.location: Palace of the Popes courtyard, Place de l'Horloge, all festival venues throughout the historic center

scams.name: Restaurant Tourist Trap Overcharging
scams.description: Some restaurants employ deceptive pricing: giving tourists English menus with higher prices, not mentioning cheaper set menus, pushing expensive bottled water when tap water is free, adding unauthorized charges to bills, and switching to cheaper wines when premium glasses are ordered.
scams.avoidance: Always ask for the French menu or both versions to compare. Request 'une carafe d'eau' for free tap water. Check if service is included. Review your bill carefully before paying.
scams.location: Place de l'Horloge, restaurants facing Palace of the Popes, tourist areas

scams.name: Les Halles Market Upselling
scams.description: Avignon's covered market Les Halles has developed a reputation for inflated prices compared to other Provence markets. Vendors may employ aggressive upselling, recommending expensive items and adding products you did not request. Prices can be 3-4 times higher than comparable markets for identical products.
scams.avoidance: Know approximate prices before shopping. Politely decline recommendations for additional items. Ask for prices before items are packaged. Visit other Provence markets for comparison.
scams.location: Les Halles d'Avignon covered market

scams.name: ATM Skimming and Card Fraud
scams.description: Criminals install card skimming devices on ATM machines to capture card details and PIN numbers. These devices blend seamlessly with normal ATM hardware. Scammers may also use fake card slot overlays that cause your card to get stuck, then offer 'help' while capturing your PIN.
scams.avoidance: Use ATMs inside banks rather than standalone machines. Cover the keypad completely when entering your PIN. Before inserting your card, inspect the machine for anything that looks crooked, loose, or damaged. Never accept help from strangers.
scams.location: Standalone ATMs in tourist areas, train stations, remote locations

scams.name: Friendship Bracelet Scam
scams.description: Scammers approach tourists and quickly weave a string bracelet around your wrist while maintaining friendly chatter. Once secured, they aggressively demand payment (often 10-20 euros). If you refuse, they may create a scene or an accomplice may use the distraction to pickpocket you.
scams.avoidance: Keep your hands in your pockets or crossed when approached. Firmly say 'non' and walk away without engaging. Never extend your hand or arm to anyone offering 'free' gifts. If tied, walk away without paying.
scams.location: Near major monuments, tourist gathering points

scams.name: Gold Ring Scam
scams.description: A scammer 'finds' a gold ring on the ground near you and offers it as your lost property or as a lucky gift. They then ask for a finder's fee (5-20 euros). Accomplices may corroborate that the ring looks valuable. The ring is actually worthless brass.
scams.avoidance: Simply walk away without engaging. Do not accept anything being 'found' near you. Ignore claims about the ring's value or religious obligations.
scams.location: Tourist walkways, gardens, along the Rhône river

scams.name: Train Station Luggage Theft
scams.description: At train stations and on trains, thieves board pretending to be passengers and wait for passengers to be distracted before grabbing bags from overhead racks and exiting just before doors close. At stations, they offer unsolicited help with luggage, then disappear with your bags.
scams.avoidance: Never separate yourself from your luggage. Keep small bags on your lap rather than in overhead racks. Use luggage locks. Politely decline help from strangers. Stay alert during boarding and at station stops.
scams.location: Avignon TGV station, Avignon Centre station, on TGV and regional trains

scams.name: Vacation Rental Fraud
scams.description: Fake vacation rental scams have increased across Provence. Scammers create attractive listings offering apartments at attractive prices, then request deposits via wire transfer outside the official platform. Tourists arrive to find the property doesn't exist or belongs to someone else.
scams.avoidance: Book only through official platforms like Airbnb or Vrbo. Never pay outside the platform or via wire transfer. Verify host profiles and reviews carefully. Be suspicious of prices that seem too good to be true.
scams.location: Online - affecting bookings throughout Avignon and Provence

scams.name: Bird Droppings Pickpocket Scam
scams.description: You're walking along the promenade near Grande Plage when suddenly something white and sticky lands on your shoulder. You look up instinctively, thinking it's bird droppings. Immediately, a 'helpful' local appears, tutting at the pigeons and offering to help clean you up. While you're distracted and they're wiping your shoulder, their accomplice is emptying your pockets or bag. The 'droppings' are actually white paste thrown by a confederate.
scams.avoidance: If substance lands on you, step away from any 'helpers' and handle it yourself. Say 'Non, merci, ca va' (No thanks, I'm fine) and move to a shop or restaurant to clean up. Keep wallet in a front pocket or secure crossbody bag that can't be accessed while you're distracted. Be suspicious of any 'helpful stranger' appearing instantly after an unexpected mishap.
scams.location: Streets near Grande Plage, Promenade du Casino, Avenue Edouard VII, pedestrian areas in city center

scams.name: Beach Blanket Theft at Grande Plage
scams.description: You've found a perfect spot on the golden sands of Grande Plage and left your bag and belongings on your beach towel while going for a quick swim in the Atlantic. In those few minutes, a thief has been watching and waiting. They casually stroll past your blanket, scoop up your phone, wallet, and keys in one fluid motion, and disappear into the crowd before you've even noticed. Beach theft spikes during July and August.
scams.avoidance: Never leave valuables unattended on the beach - use a waterproof pouch to take essentials into the water. Leave passport, excess cash, and electronics in your hotel safe before heading to the beach. Swim in shifts with companions so someone always watches belongings. Position yourself near lifeguard stations where surveillance is higher.
scams.location: Grande Plage, Plage Miramar, Cote des Basques, beach areas during peak summer season

scams.name: Camera Drop Scam
scams.description: You're admiring the stunning view from Rocher de la Vierge when a friendly tourist asks if you'd take their photo with their nice-looking camera. You oblige, and as you hand the camera back, they fumble it dramatically and it crashes to the ground. They examine their 'broken' camera and start demanding you pay for the damage - €200-300 or more. The camera was already broken or is a cheap prop.
scams.avoidance: It's fine to take photos for tourists, but hand the camera back carefully and step back before releasing. If they drop it, remember the fumble was on their end. Never pay cash on the spot; suggest involving police if they claim damage. Walk away if they become aggressive.
scams.location: Rocher de la Vierge viewpoint, Port Vieux, Grande Plage promenade, popular photo spots

scams.name: ATM Card Skimming and Shoulder Surfing
scams.description: You're withdrawing cash from an ATM near the casino when someone approaches offering helpful advice about fees. While they 'help,' they're watching you enter your PIN and may have a card skimmer in their pocket scanning your card's magnetic strip. Or they've already installed a skimmer on the ATM slot itself. Days later, your account shows unauthorized withdrawals in eastern Europe.
scams.avoidance: Use ATMs inside banks during business hours where tampering is less likely. Cover the keypad completely with your hand when entering your PIN. Check the card slot by wiggling it gently - skimmers are often loosely attached. Never accept help from strangers at ATMs.
scams.location: ATMs near Casino Barriere, Avenue Edouard VII, Les Halles market area, train station

scams.name: Shell Game and Three-Card Monte
scams.description: You spot a small crowd gathered around a man with three boxes or cards on a folding table near the casino promenade. He's shuffling them rapidly, inviting people to guess which one hides the ball. Someone in the crowd bets €20 and wins easily. But those 'winners' are accomplices working with the operator. The moment you put money down, sleight of hand ensures you lose. Meanwhile, pickpockets work the crowd.
scams.avoidance: Never gamble with street operators - the games are rigged without exception. Walk past quickly without stopping to watch; observation makes you a target. Remember that every 'winner' you see is a plant working with the scammer. Keep hands on your valuables if you even pause near a street game.
scams.location: Casino promenade, Grande Plage boardwalk, near Rocher de la Vierge during peak tourist season

scams.name: Friendly Bar Overcharging Scam
scams.description: You're enjoying an evening when two attractive locals strike up a friendly conversation and suggest drinks at a place they know nearby. After a couple of drinks, the bill arrives: €150-200 or more for what seemed like a few cocktails. The drinks were massively inflated 'tourist prices,' and your 'friends' chip in only a token amount before disappearing. Large bouncers may escort you to an ATM if you protest.
scams.avoidance: Choose your own venues - never let strangers guide you to a bar they recommend. Always check prices before ordering; no posted prices is a massive red flag. Suggest well-known, established bars if new acquaintances want drinks. If confronted with an outrageous bill, insist on calling police before paying.
scams.location: Bars near Port Vieux, late-night establishments in city center, venues off main tourist streets

scams.name: Les Halles Market Pickpocketing
scams.description: Les Halles is a beloved Biarritz institution where locals and tourists jostle to buy fresh seafood and regional specialties. The crowded aisles, sensory overload, and tourists fumbling with euros make it a prime hunting ground for skilled pickpockets. While you're admiring the piment d'Espelette display or counting change, a bump passes unnoticed - and your wallet goes with it.
scams.avoidance: Wear a crossbody bag with the opening against your body, hand resting on top. Keep wallet in a front pocket, never in a backpack or rear pocket. Bring only the cash you need for market purchases; leave cards at the hotel. Be extra vigilant during peak Saturday morning hours.
scams.location: Les Halles de Biarritz indoor market, Saturday morning market, Rue des Halles area

scams.name: Unlicensed Taxi Overcharging
scams.description: You've just landed at Biarritz Airport after a long journey, and as you exit arrivals, a friendly man approaches offering a taxi into town. He quotes €40 - but this isn't an official taxi. Once in the car, the price might increase, or you're taken on a scenic route. Official airport taxis should cost around €25 to central Biarritz. Unlicensed operators charge double or triple the standard fare.
scams.avoidance: Use only official taxis from the designated taxi rank at the airport or station. Look for official taxi signage, license numbers on windshield, and running meters. Know the expected fare in advance: airport to city center is approximately €25. Use ride-hailing apps for transparent pricing.
scams.location: Biarritz-Pays Basque Airport (BIQ), Biarritz train station, late-night casino area

scams.name: Fake Charity Petition Scam
scams.description: You're strolling along the promenade when a young woman approaches with a clipboard, gesturing that she's deaf-mute. She wants you to sign a petition for disabled children or another worthy cause. Once signed, she flips to a donation page showing €20-50 amounts. Meanwhile, your attention is on the clipboard, making you an easy mark for an accomplice to pickpocket. The charity doesn't exist.
scams.avoidance: Politely decline with 'Non, merci' and keep walking without breaking stride. Never sign anything on the street; legitimate charities don't solicit signatures on promenades. Keep your hands occupied with bags or phone so you can't take the clipboard. Genuine charities have websites, offices, and don't rely on street solicitation.
scams.location: Grande Plage promenade, Place Clemenceau, near the casino, pedestrian shopping areas

scams.name: Remote Beach and Parking Lot Car Break-Ins
scams.description: You've driven to one of Biarritz's stunning remote beaches for an afternoon of surfing or sunbathing. You leave your rental car in the parking lot with your bags hidden in the boot. But thieves stake out these beach parking areas, watching tourists head down to the water. Within minutes, they've smashed a window or popped a lock. Valuables 'hidden' in the boot are found quickly.
scams.avoidance: Leave all valuables at your hotel - don't bring anything to the beach you can't carry into the water. Use paid, supervised parking lots rather than remote free parking when possible. If you must leave items in the car, put them in the boot BEFORE arriving at the beach. Don't leave any bags visible in the car, even if they contain nothing valuable.
scams.location: Cote des Basques parking lot, Plage de la Milady parking, remote surf spot access roads, cliffside parking areas

scams.name: Pickpocketing in Tourist Areas
scams.description: Pickpockets operate in crowded tourist areas throughout Bordeaux, particularly at Place de la Bourse, along Rue Sainte-Catherine (one of Europe's longest pedestrian shopping streets), and near the Miroir d'Eau. Thieves work in teams, using distraction techniques while accomplices steal wallets, phones, and valuables. They often target tourists who are taking photos or consulting maps.
scams.avoidance: Use anti-theft bags with hidden compartments. Keep wallets in front pockets, never back pockets. Avoid displaying expensive jewelry or electronics. Stay alert in crowded areas. Keep bags zipped and in front of your body.
scams.location: Place de la Bourse, Rue Sainte-Catherine, Miroir d'Eau, tourist landmarks

scams.name: Train Station Theft
scams.description: Bordeaux Saint-Jean train station attracts pickpockets who target confused tourists carrying luggage. A common tactic involves groups of 4-6 people pushing onto trains just before doors close, crowding targets while accomplices steal valuables, then hopping off as doors close. Thieves also operate near ticket machines and in crowded platform areas.
scams.avoidance: Keep bags in front of you and secured at all times. Be extra vigilant when boarding trains. Don't put phones or wallets in easily accessible pockets. Watch for people crowding you unnecessarily. Board trains early rather than rushing at the last moment.
scams.location: Gare de Bordeaux Saint-Jean, train platforms, ticket areas

scams.name: The Petition Clipboard Scam
scams.description: Scammers approach tourists with clipboards asking them to sign a petition, often claiming to support deaf children or a charitable cause. While the tourist is distracted reading and signing, an accomplice steals their wallet, phone, or valuables from bags or pockets. Sometimes the petitioner themselves will demand a donation after signing, becoming aggressive if refused.
scams.avoidance: Politely decline and keep walking. Never stop for clipboard solicitors. Keep hands on your belongings. Say 'non merci' firmly while continuing to move. Never sign anything on the street.
scams.location: Tourist areas, near monuments, pedestrian zones

scams.name: The Friendship Bracelet Trap
scams.description: A stranger approaches and begins tying a colorful string bracelet on your wrist as a supposed 'gift' or sign of friendship. Once the bracelet is tied, they aggressively demand payment, often 10-20 euros. They refuse to take the bracelet back and may create a scene to pressure payment. Meanwhile, accomplices may use the distraction to pickpocket you.
scams.avoidance: Keep your hands in your pockets or crossed. Firmly refuse any 'gifts' from strangers. Say 'non' and walk away quickly. Never let strangers touch your hands or wrists. If a bracelet is tied, refuse to pay and walk toward police.
scams.location: Tourist areas, near cafes and restaurants, pedestrian zones

scams.name: The Gold Ring Trick
scams.description: A scammer pretends to 'find' a gold ring on the ground near you and insists you should have it, claiming it doesn't fit them or suggesting you can sell it. They then ask for a small finder's fee or payment. The ring is worthless brass or fake gold. This scam is particularly common throughout France and targets tourists who appear kind or confused.
scams.avoidance: Ignore anyone who approaches with a 'found' ring. Keep walking without engaging. Say 'Ce n'est pas à moi' (It's not mine) and walk away. Remember that real gold rings are never given away by strangers.
scams.location: Near tourist attractions, parks, riverside walkways

scams.name: Fake Police Wallet Inspection
scams.description: Scammers posing as plainclothes police officers flash fake badges and demand to inspect your wallet for 'counterfeit currency.' They work in pairs: one may pretend to be a drug dealer to engage you, then the fake officer appears to 'investigate.' While examining your cash, they palm bills. Real French police never ask to see your wallet contents on the street.
scams.avoidance: Real police only ask to see ID documents, not wallets. Request to see official identification clearly. Insist on going to the nearest police station. Call 17 (police) if uncertain. Never hand over your wallet to anyone on the street.
scams.location: Tourist areas, metro stations, busy streets

scams.name: Unlicensed Taxi Overcharging
scams.description: Unlicensed taxi drivers approach tourists at Bordeaux-Merignac Airport or Gare Saint-Jean, offering rides at inflated prices. They may claim there's a taxi strike or that official taxis are unavailable. These unofficial drivers can charge 2-3 times the normal fare and may not be insured. Some use rigged meters or claim the meter is broken.
scams.avoidance: Only use taxis from official taxi ranks. Look for vehicles with official taxi signage and roof lights. Use ride-sharing apps like Uber or Bolt for transparent pricing. Always confirm the fare before getting in. Note the driver's license number displayed in the vehicle.
scams.location: Bordeaux-Merignac Airport, Gare Saint-Jean train station

scams.name: Restaurant Menu Overcharging
scams.description: Some restaurants in tourist areas show tourists different menus with higher prices, add hidden charges for bread, water, or table settings, or charge for items not ordered. Staff may also substitute cheaper wine when premium glasses are ordered. Bills may include undisclosed service charges or inflated prices for tourists, especially Americans.
scams.avoidance: Check that menus display prices (legally required in France). Compare printed menu prices to your bill. Ask 'une carafe d'eau' for free tap water. Verify wine bottle labels match what you ordered. Avoid restaurants without posted prices.
scams.location: Tourist areas, restaurants near major attractions

scams.name: ATM Skimming and Card Theft
scams.description: Criminals install skimming devices on ATMs to capture card details and PINs. These devices blend with the ATM's original hardware and are hard to detect. Scammers also use distraction techniques: one person engages you while another watches you enter your PIN or manipulates the machine to trap your card.
scams.avoidance: Use ATMs inside banks during business hours. Inspect card slots for loose attachments. Cover keypad when entering PIN. Never accept help from strangers at ATMs. If card is trapped, don't leave and call your bank immediately.
scams.location: Tourist areas, train stations, shopping districts

scams.name: Rose Seller Scam
scams.description: Men approach couples or women at restaurant terraces and outdoor cafes, offering a 'free' rose as a romantic gesture. Once the rose is accepted or touched, they aggressively demand payment of 5-10 euros. They refuse to take the rose back and create uncomfortable confrontations. Sometimes accomplices use this distraction to pickpocket victims.
scams.avoidance: Decline firmly and keep your hands away. Avoid touching offered items. Say 'non merci' without stopping. Alert restaurant staff if sellers become aggressive.
scams.location: Restaurant terraces, outdoor cafes, riverside areas, romantic spots

scams.name: Tram and Bus Pickpocketing
scams.description: Pickpockets operate on Bordeaux's tram network and buses, particularly during rush hours and on routes serving tourist areas. Thieves create distractions by bumping into victims or 'helping' with bags while accomplices steal valuables. At stops near tourist destinations, thieves may grab phones or bags just as doors are closing.
scams.avoidance: Keep valuables in front pockets or secure inside bags. Stay alert especially near doors. Be wary of anyone offering unsolicited help. Avoid standing near doors with easily accessible items.
scams.location: Bordeaux tram lines, buses, stops near tourist attractions

scams.name: Fake Accommodation Listings
scams.description: Scammers create fake Airbnb or rental listings using photos from legitimate properties, offering attractive prices in desirable locations. They request payment via wire transfer or cryptocurrency outside the official platform, then disappear. Tourists arrive to find the property doesn't exist or belongs to someone else. France is a hotspot for this scam.
scams.avoidance: Only book through official platforms and pay through their systems. Be suspicious of unusually low prices. Never wire money directly. Verify listings have reviews and host history. Use Google Street View to verify property exists.
scams.location: Online booking platforms, social media advertisements

scams.name: Luxury Watch Theft
scams.description: Organized criminal groups specifically target tourists wearing expensive watches worth over $100,000. Spotters identify valuable timepieces like Rolex and Patek Philippe, then signal to accomplices who snatch the watch and flee on mopeds with tampered plates. In 2024, the Alpes-Maritimes region recorded 301 watches stolen totaling $8.3 million. Attacks can involve tear gas or violence.
scams.avoidance: Leave expensive watches at home or in your hotel safe. If you must wear one, keep it concealed under long sleeves. Be especially vigilant on restaurant terraces and near luxury hotels. Sit with your back to the wall when dining.
scams.location: La Croisette, Port Canto, hotel terraces, restaurant patios, luxury shopping areas

scams.name: Taxi Meter Manipulation
scams.description: Despite fixed rates from Nice Airport (€85 to Cannes), some taxi drivers start with the fixed rate already on the meter and then let it continue running, effectively charging double. Drivers may claim credit card machines are broken to force cash payment without a receipt, enabling overcharging.
scams.avoidance: Confirm the fixed rate before entering the taxi and photograph the meter at the start. Insist on a receipt and credit card payment. Use official taxi ranks at the airport. Consider Uber where available.
scams.location: Nice Airport, Cannes train station, hotels

scams.name: Pickpocketing with Distraction
scams.description: Professional pickpockets work in teams of three or more: one creates a distraction by asking for directions, spilling something on you, or creating a commotion, while accomplices steal your belongings. Train stations and boarding areas are particularly vulnerable spots.
scams.avoidance: Use a money belt or anti-theft bag. Keep valuables in front pockets. Stay alert when anyone approaches unexpectedly. If something is spilled on you, move away from 'helpful' strangers before addressing it.
scams.location: Cannes train station, La Croisette, Palais des Festivals, crowded markets

scams.name: Petition and Charity Clipboard Scam
scams.description: Scammers, often pretending to be deaf and mute, approach tourists with clipboards asking them to sign petitions for fake charities. After signing, they demand donations of €2-10. While your hands are occupied signing, accomplices may pickpocket your belongings.
scams.avoidance: Politely but firmly decline and keep walking. Never sign anything presented by strangers on the street. Keep your hands free and your belongings secured.
scams.location: La Croisette, Palais des Festivals area, tourist hotspots, near train stations

scams.name: Gold Ring Scam
scams.description: A scammer 'finds' a gold ring on the ground near you and offers to sell it at a discount. The ring is actually worthless brass or copper, often stamped with fake 18K markings. They create urgency by claiming they need money immediately.
scams.avoidance: Never buy jewelry from strangers on the street. If someone tries to give you a 'found' ring, decline immediately and walk away.
scams.location: Tourist areas, La Croisette, near beaches

scams.name: Friendship Bracelet Scam
scams.description: Scammers approach tourists and quickly tie colorful string bracelets around their wrists, making them difficult to remove. They then aggressively demand payment of €10-20. While the victim is distracted, an accomplice may steal wallets or phones.
scams.avoidance: Keep your hands in your pockets or crossed when approached by street vendors. Firmly say 'Non, merci' and walk away immediately.
scams.location: La Croisette, Palais des Festivals, crowded pedestrian areas

scams.name: Beach Club Overcharging
scams.description: Some private beach clubs add unauthorized charges to bills, including inflated prices for basic items. Staff may aggressively enforce rules about outside food, confiscating items and pressuring customers to buy expensive alternatives. Hidden 'service charges' may appear on final bills.
scams.avoidance: Ask for a complete price list before ordering and confirm all charges upfront. Keep all receipts and check your bill carefully before paying. Choose established beach clubs with good reviews.
scams.location: Private beach clubs along La Croisette, Plage du Midi

scams.name: Restaurant Menu Tricks
scams.description: Some restaurants use deceptive pricing including dual menus with higher prices for tourists, omitting prices for daily specials that turn out expensive, and adding unauthorized cover charges. Fish may be priced per 100 grams rather than per portion, leading to shocking bills.
scams.avoidance: Always ask for prices of specials before ordering. Request to see the menu with prices. Check if service is included. Check reviews before dining.
scams.location: Le Suquet old town, restaurants near Palais des Festivals, tourist-heavy areas

scams.name: Fake Police Officer Scam
scams.description: Criminals pose as plainclothes police officers and approach tourists, claiming to conduct ID or currency checks. They ask to see your wallet to 'verify' your money isn't counterfeit, then steal cash or the entire wallet. Real French police rarely approach tourists on the street for such checks.
scams.avoidance: Legitimate French police almost never approach tourists for random currency checks. Never hand over your wallet. Ask to see police credentials and suggest going to a police station together. Call 17 if threatened.
scams.location: Tourist areas, near ATMs, hotel entrances

scams.name: ATM Skimming and Shimming
scams.description: Criminals install nearly invisible 'shimming' devices inside ATM card slots that capture data from your card's chip. These devices use Bluetooth or cellular connections to transmit stolen data. Some criminals also install hidden cameras to capture PIN codes.
scams.avoidance: Use ATMs inside banks during banking hours. Cover the keypad when entering your PIN. Inspect the card slot for anything loose or unusual. Enable transaction alerts on your accounts.
scams.location: Standalone ATMs, tourist areas, train stations, outside nightclubs

scams.name: Vacation Rental Fraud
scams.description: Scammers create fake listings for properties that don't exist or aren't available, using stolen photos. They insist on payment outside official platforms like Airbnb. Victims discover upon arrival that their reservation doesn't exist. Particularly common during the Film Festival when demand peaks.
scams.avoidance: Only book through reputable platforms and never pay outside the official system. Be suspicious of prices significantly below market rate, especially during Film Festival. Verify listings have reviews.
scams.location: Online booking platforms, especially during Cannes Film Festival period

scams.name: Film Festival Credential Scams
scams.description: Fake websites and social media accounts offer Film Festival passes, party invitations, or screening tickets at inflated prices for events that don't exist. Scammers also target filmmakers with fake festivals charging high submission fees. Some fake internship programs charge thousands for worthless 'festival experience' programs.
scams.avoidance: Purchase tickets and passes only through official Cannes Film Festival channels (festival-cannes.com). Research any festival carefully before paying fees. Verify internship programs through educational institutions.
scams.location: Online, around Palais des Festivals during Festival period

scams.name: Yacht Charter Fraud
scams.description: Fraudulent yacht charter companies advertise luxury boats they don't own, taking large deposits and disappearing. Warning signs include companies with only mobile phone contacts, no physical address, pressure to pay quickly, and unusually low prices.
scams.avoidance: Book only with established charter companies with physical offices. Verify membership in professional organizations like MYBA or ECPY. Never pay large deposits to unverified companies. Meet the boat and crew before final payment if possible.
scams.location: Online booking sites, Port de Cannes, Port Canto

scams.name: Car Break-In Theft
scams.description: Thieves target rental cars parked at beaches, hiking trailheads, and tourist sites, recognizing rental vehicles by their license plates. They break windows to steal valuables in seconds, targeting cameras, electronics, luggage, and passports.
scams.avoidance: Never leave anything visible in your car. Remove all belongings when parking, even briefly. Use monitored parking garages rather than street parking. Keep important documents on your person.
scams.location: Beach parking areas, hiking trailheads, scenic viewpoints, rural parking spots

scams.name: Fake Chalet Rental Scam
scams.description: Scammers screenshot photos of legitimate luxury chalets and create fake listings at suspiciously low prices during peak winter season. They request immediate wire transfers for deposits and first month's rent, often claiming high demand requires fast action. Once payment is sent, the scammer disappears and victims arrive to find the property either doesn't exist or is occupied by the real owner. This is the most widespread scam affecting visitors to Chamonix.
scams.avoidance: Book through established agencies like Chamonix All Year or verified platforms. Never wire money to individuals without seeing the property. Use credit cards for payment protection. Verify property addresses on Google Street View. Join local Facebook groups like Cham Social for recommendations.
scams.location: Online listings targeting Chamonix town center, Les Praz, Argentière, and popular ski-in/ski-out areas

scams.name: Unlicensed Mountain Guide Scam
scams.description: Fake 'mountain guides' advertise online with fabricated testimonials and impressive credentials, charging €1,500 or more for Mont Blanc summit attempts. These unqualified individuals have abandoned exhausted clients in dangerous conditions near high-altitude refuges, leaving them stranded in snowstorms. Without proper insurance coverage, victims have no recourse for compensation if accidents occur.
scams.avoidance: Book only through Compagnie des Guides de Chamonix or IFMGA-certified guides. Ask to see the guide's UIAGM/IFMGA identification card. Verify guide credentials on official mountain guide registries. Use established mountain guiding companies with insurance guarantees.
scams.location: Online bookings for Mont Blanc ascents, Aiguille du Midi departures, Goûter Route, Refuge de Tête Rousse area

scams.name: Fake Ski Instructor Scam
scams.description: Unqualified individuals pose as ski instructors online, offering lessons at discounted rates compared to ESF (École du Ski Français). Some take advance payment and never appear, while others actually conduct lessons without proper certification. Victims who take lessons from unqualified instructors face serious safety risks on challenging Alpine terrain and have no insurance coverage. French courts have fined operators over €26,000 for employing unlicensed instructors.
scams.avoidance: Book through ESF Chamonix or other licensed ski schools. Verify instructor certifications through official channels. Ask for proof of insurance before lessons begin. Check reviews on established booking platforms.
scams.location: Online bookings, Brévent-Flégère area, Les Grands Montets, Chamonix town meeting points

scams.name: Ski Equipment Theft at Slopes
scams.description: Opportunistic thieves target expensive ski equipment left unattended on racks outside mountain restaurants and lodges. The 'snatch and grab' technique accounts for 90% of ski thefts, where criminals identify desirable equipment on one pass and return to steal it quickly. High-end skis, boots, and poles worth thousands of euros are stolen within minutes while owners enjoy lunch inside.
scams.avoidance: Use ski locks with cables at least 4mm thick. Separate your skis and store them in different rack locations. Leave skis in less crowded areas away from main entrances. Use resort locker facilities like Skicase in Chamonix. Purchase rental insurance that covers theft.
scams.location: Ski racks outside restaurants at Planpraz, La Flégère, Les Grands Montets base lodge, Brévent summit restaurant, Le 3842 restaurant at Aiguille du Midi

scams.name: Booking Platform Accommodation Fraud
scams.description: Guests book legitimate-appearing properties through major platforms but encounter unexpected demands upon arrival. In documented Chamonix cases, hosts have held guests 'hostage' demanding additional cash deposits of €400 or more that were never mentioned in the listing and never returned. Some properties advertised as ski-in/ski-out turn out to be far from slopes.
scams.avoidance: Only communicate and pay through official booking platform channels. Read all reviews carefully, especially recent negative ones. Verify exact property location on maps before booking. Document all communications and demands in writing. Report unusual demands immediately to the booking platform.
scams.location: Properties listed on Booking.com, Airbnb for Chamonix center and surrounding villages

scams.name: Defective SIM Card Scam
scams.description: Tourists purchase prepaid SIM cards marketed as 5G service with 14 days of calls and data for €34. The SIM cards stop working within hours of purchase, and when customers contact the carrier (such as Orange), they discover the SIM was already deactivated or never properly activated. Shop owners claim no responsibility.
scams.avoidance: Purchase SIM cards from official carrier stores (Orange, SFR, Bouygues). Ask seller to activate and test the SIM before completing purchase. Keep all receipts and packaging. Consider purchasing SIM cards at Geneva Airport before arrival.
scams.location: Tabac shops and convenience stores near Gare de Chamonix-Mont-Blanc

scams.name: Unlicensed Airport Transfer Overcharging
scams.description: Unofficial taxi drivers approach tourists at Geneva Airport offering transfers to Chamonix at seemingly reasonable rates. Once en route, they demand significantly higher fees, sometimes claiming the original quote was per person not per vehicle, or adding fuel surcharges and border crossing fees. Some drivers refuse to cross into France, abandoning passengers at the border.
scams.avoidance: Pre-book transfers through established companies like Alpine Fleet or Chamonix Cabs. Use official shared shuttle services (€30-40 per person). Get written confirmation of total price including all fees. Book private transfers that average €150-200 for the journey.
scams.location: Geneva Airport arrivals area, unofficial taxi ranks, online booking sites for Geneva-Chamonix transfers

scams.name: Gold Ring Scam
scams.description: A person 'finds' a gold ring on the ground near you and offers to sell it at a 'discounted' price since they don't need it. The ring is actually worthless brass or plated metal. While this scam is more common in Paris and larger French cities, it appears in mountain resort towns during peak season when wealthy tourists are concentrated.
scams.avoidance: Politely refuse and walk away immediately. Never engage in conversation about found items. Understand that real gold rings aren't sold by strangers on streets.
scams.location: Chamonix town center pedestrian areas, near Place Balmat, along Rue du Docteur Paccard

scams.name: Fake Police Officer Scam
scams.description: Individuals impersonate plainclothes police officers and approach tourists, claiming to conduct anti-counterfeiting operations or security checks. They ask to see identification, wallets, or search belongings, using the opportunity to steal cash, cards, or valuables. Some work in teams where one distracts while another pickpockets.
scams.avoidance: Ask to see official police credentials. Offer to accompany them to the nearest police station. Never hand over your wallet - show ID through clear wallet pocket. Call 17 (French police) if suspicious.
scams.location: Tourist areas throughout Chamonix, near ATMs, Place Balmat, parking areas

scams.name: Counterfeit Ski Pass Sales
scams.description: Scammers sell counterfeit or stolen ski passes at discounted prices, either online before arrival or near lift stations. These passes may be altered legitimate passes with dates whited out, child passes being sold for adult use, or completely counterfeited tickets. Victims are caught at lift gates, face fines up to €999, and lose their payment.
scams.avoidance: Purchase passes only from official Compagnie du Mont-Blanc outlets. Buy online through official Chamonix lift company website. Never buy passes from individuals at the resort. Keep receipts as proof of legitimate purchase.
scams.location: Online marketplaces, Chamonix town center, near lift station entrances at Aiguille du Midi, Brévent, Les Grands Montets

scams.name: Cable Car Crowding Pickpocketing
scams.description: During peak season and holiday periods, the famous cable cars become extremely crowded with tourists focused on the spectacular views. Pickpockets take advantage of the tight quarters and distracted visitors to steal wallets, phones, and valuables. The Aiguille du Midi cable car, carrying up to 65 passengers in a small space, is particularly vulnerable.
scams.avoidance: Keep valuables in front pockets or secure money belt. Use bags with zippers worn across your body in front. Be extra vigilant during boarding and crowded moments. Leave unnecessary valuables in hotel safe.
scams.location: Aiguille du Midi cable car queues and cars, Panoramic Mont-Blanc gondola, Brévent télécabine during peak hours

scams.name: Restaurant Tourist Trap Overcharging
scams.description: Some restaurants in prime tourist locations employ tactics to overcharge visitors: presenting menus without prices, automatically adding expensive bottled water instead of free tap water, charging inflated 'terrace supplements,' adding undisclosed service charges, or bringing unrequested items and then charging premium prices.
scams.avoidance: Always request a menu with prices before ordering. Ask specifically for 'une carafe d'eau' (tap water) which is free. Confirm prices for daily specials before ordering. Check the bill carefully before paying.
scams.location: Restaurants near Place Balmat, Rue du Docteur Paccard, slopes-adjacent establishments at Planpraz and Brévent

scams.name: Train Station Luggage Helper Theft
scams.description: Organized groups of thieves operate at Colmar train station, posing as helpful strangers offering to assist tourists with their luggage. Two or three young individuals approach travelers on stairs or near platforms, insisting on helping carry bags despite refusals. While one person distracts with conversation or blocks your view, another rifles through bags or pockets, stealing passports, wallets, and valuables.
scams.avoidance: Firmly decline all unsolicited help with luggage. Ask station staff in red tabards for assistance if needed. Keep bags zipped and secured in front of your body. Travel with only luggage you can manage alone.
scams.location: Colmar train station (Gare de Colmar), platform stairs, luggage areas

scams.name: Christmas Market Pickpocketing
scams.description: During Colmar's famous Christmas markets (late November through December), professional pickpockets work the dense crowds moving between market stalls. Victims often report having wallets stolen from zipped crossbody purses or coat pockets while navigating the narrow medieval streets packed with holiday shoppers. The crush of tourists photographing half-timbered houses creates perfect cover for skilled thieves.
scams.avoidance: Wear crossbody bags in front of your body with locking zippers. Keep wallets in front pockets or money belts under clothing. Visit markets Monday-Thursday when crowds are lighter. Avoid peak weekend hours between 11am-5pm.
scams.location: Colmar Christmas Markets, Place des Dominicains, Place de l'Ancienne Douane, Petite Venise, medieval Old Town pedestrian streets

scams.name: Restaurant Tourist Menu Overcharging
scams.description: Certain restaurants in Colmar's heavily-touristed areas engage in deceptive pricing practices. Visitors have reported being charged 7 euros extra per person when attempting to share a menu. Other tactics include presenting tourists with different menus featuring inflated prices, adding undisclosed charges for bread or water, or bringing unrequested items and billing for them.
scams.avoidance: Check prices on posted menus before sitting down. Eat where locals eat - venture a few streets from main tourist paths. Review recent TripAdvisor and Google reviews before dining. Ask for itemized bill and verify all charges match menu prices.
scams.location: Little Venice (Petite Venise), Place de l'Ancienne Douane, Rue des Marchands, areas near Maison Pfister

scams.name: Fake Petition/Deaf Charity Scam
scams.description: Groups of individuals approach tourists with clipboards, asking them to sign petitions for fake charitable causes, often pretending to be deaf-mute. The petitions are typically in English (suspicious in a French city) and claim to support disabled people. After signing, they reveal a 'donation' column and pressure you for 10-20 euros. While you're distracted, an accomplice may be pickpocketing you.
scams.avoidance: Say 'Non, merci' firmly and keep walking without stopping. Never sign anything offered by strangers on the street. Keep your bag secured in front of you if approached. Remember that legitimate charities don't solicit cash on streets.
scams.location: Colmar train station area, Place Rapp, near Musee Unterlinden, Cathedral of Saint Martin, tourist walking areas

scams.name: ATM Skimming and Card Fraud
scams.description: France experiences 42% of all European bank card fraud. Criminals install skimming devices on ATMs that capture card data and hidden cameras or keypad overlays that record PIN entries. Tourist areas are prime targets because foreign cards are less likely to have advanced security features. Victims typically discover the theft weeks later when unauthorized charges appear on their statements.
scams.avoidance: Use ATMs inside banks during business hours only. Inspect the card slot and keypad before inserting card - wiggle the slot. Always cover your hand when entering PIN. Set up transaction alerts on your cards before traveling.
scams.location: Standalone ATMs in tourist areas, train station ATMs, ATMs on Rue des Marchands, machines near Christmas markets

scams.name: Fake Police Officer Scam
scams.description: Scammers pose as plainclothes police officers, quickly flashing fake badges and demanding to 'check your documents and wallet for counterfeit currency.' While examining your wallet, they palm cash or memorize card details. Some wear partial uniforms or hats with police markings to appear legitimate. French authorities have warned about increased incidents of criminals impersonating officers.
scams.avoidance: Know that real French police will NEVER demand your wallet, cash, or phone. Ask to see proper identification and request their serial number. Suggest going to the nearest police station together for any document checks. Call 17 (police emergency) if unsure about legitimacy.
scams.location: Colmar train station, parking areas near Old Town, near tourist attractions, quiet side streets

scams.name: QR Code Parking Meter Scam (Quishing)
scams.description: Scammers place fake QR code stickers over legitimate ones on parking meters throughout France. When tourists scan the fraudulent code, they're directed to a convincing phishing website that mimics official parking payment services. Victims enter their license plate, parking duration, and credit card details - all captured by criminals. Some victims are tricked into entering multiple card numbers after being told their payment 'failed.'
scams.avoidance: Run your finger over QR codes to detect if it's a sticker covering another code. Type parking payment URLs directly rather than scanning codes. Use official parking apps downloaded from app stores, not QR links. Pay at meter using coin or chip-enabled card rather than QR when possible.
scams.location: Public parking meters throughout Colmar, parking areas near Old Town, tourist parking zones

scams.name: Wine Tasting Pressure Sales
scams.description: While wine tastings along the Alsace Wine Route often appear free, there's strong social pressure to purchase bottles afterward. Some establishments serve generous pours to lower inhibitions, create false scarcity ('last bottles of this vintage'), or make tourists feel obligated after extensive tastings. Staff may become noticeably cold or hostile if visitors don't make purchases.
scams.avoidance: Look for 'Vignobles et Decouvertes' certified wineries for quality assurance. Set a budget before entering any cave and stick to it. Know it's perfectly acceptable to taste and buy just one bottle or none at all. Ask about tasting fees upfront before sampling begins.
scams.location: Alsace Wine Route villages (Eguisheim, Riquewihr, Kaysersberg), small caves in Colmar, roadside tasting rooms

scams.name: Rental Car Break-In Theft
scams.description: Thieves specifically target rental cars parked at tourist attractions throughout Alsace. They watch parking lots for tourists who open their trunks to store or retrieve items, marking which vehicles contain valuables. Rental cars are easily identified by registration stickers, missing floor mats, and clean interiors. Travelers return from wine tastings to find windows smashed and all belongings stolen.
scams.avoidance: Never open your trunk in the parking lot where thieves might see contents. Retrieve needed items a mile before arriving at destination. Remove all visible items including guidebooks, maps, and ticket stubs. Use underground or multistorey car parks with CCTV when possible.
scams.location: Tourist parking areas along Wine Route, parking lots at village viewpoints, free parking zones near attractions, trailhead parking

scams.name: Fake Accommodation Booking Scam
scams.description: Scammers create fake listings mimicking real Colmar properties on platforms like Airbnb and Booking.com, or send phishing emails claiming your reservation was cancelled with large penalty charges. Colmar's picturesque half-timbered houses make it easy to steal photos for convincing fake listings. Victims arrive to find their 'charming Alsatian apartment' doesn't exist.
scams.avoidance: Book only through official platforms and pay within their secure system. Verify emails by logging into booking sites directly, never via email links. Cross-reference property photos using reverse image search. Read reviews carefully and look for specific details about Colmar location.
scams.location: Online platforms, fake booking websites, phishing emails

scams.name: Pickpocketing
scams.description: Pickpockets in Lyon operate in tourist-heavy areas and on crowded public transport. They often work in teams using distraction techniques - one person might ask for directions, bump into you, or create a commotion while an accomplice steals your wallet or phone. At the Confluence Tram stop, groups of women wearing large bags have been observed surrounding tourists to access backpacks. On metro Line D and the T2 tram, pickpockets are most active during rush hour boarding and exiting when movement is chaotic.
scams.avoidance: Wear bags across your body with zippers facing inward. Keep only minimal cash and one card on you. Use money belts or hidden pouches. Stay alert during metro boarding and exiting.
scams.location: Vieux Lyon, Place Bellecour, Part-Dieu station, Perrache station, Confluence Tram stop, Metro Line D, T2 tram line, Basilica of Notre-Dame de Fourvière

scams.name: Fake Metro Ticket Scam
scams.description: Ticket touts approach tourists who appear lost or confused at major Lyon train stations. They offer to sell metro tickets at seemingly reasonable prices, but the tickets are either fake, expired, or already used. The scammer may claim they have 'extra' tickets or offer a 'discount' compared to the official ticket machines. When you try to use the ticket, it won't work at the turnstile.
scams.avoidance: Only buy tickets from official TCL machines or counters. Use the TCL mobile app for digital tickets. Ignore anyone offering to sell tickets outside official channels.
scams.location: Part-Dieu station, Perrache station

scams.name: Fake Charity/Petition Scam
scams.description: Someone approaches with a clipboard asking 'Do you speak English?' and requests you sign a petition for a charity supporting deaf-mute individuals. After signing, they flip the clipboard to reveal a donation section and pressure you to give money. While you're distracted with the clipboard, an accomplice may pickpocket you from behind.
scams.avoidance: Simply say 'Non, merci' and keep walking. Never sign anything handed to you on the street. Legitimate charities in France only ask for email addresses, not cash.
scams.location: Rue de la République, Part-Dieu station, Perrache station, Place Bellecour

scams.name: Restaurant Overcharging
scams.description: Tourist-centric restaurants near Lyon's historic areas may present inflated bills. Tactics include: adding items you didn't order, charging for bread and water that appeared 'free,' using 'tourist menus' with elevated prices. Some establishments trade on Lyon's reputation as France's gastronomic capital to justify excessive prices for mediocre food.
scams.avoidance: Check prices before sitting down. Ask for itemized bills and review carefully. Eat where locals eat, away from main tourist streets.
scams.location: Vieux Lyon (Old Town), Presqu'île, Rue Mercière

scams.name: Shell Game / Three-Card Monte
scams.description: A scammer sets up a makeshift table with three cups or cards. They invite you to bet on guessing the ball's location. 'Winners' in the crowd are accomplices who pretend to win to draw you in. The game is completely rigged through sleight of hand - you cannot win.
scams.avoidance: Never play street gambling games - they are always rigged. Do not stop to watch. Remember that bystanders are likely accomplices.
scams.location: Busy tourist areas, Near major attractions, Metro exits

scams.name: Gold Ring Scam
scams.description: A person 'finds' a gold ring on the ground near you and asks if you dropped it. When you say no, they show you a marking claiming it's real gold and offer to sell it for a 'good price.' The ring is worthless brass. They may also ask for money 'for food' or 'for their children.'
scams.avoidance: Don't engage - say 'Non' and keep walking. Never accept items 'found' on the street.
scams.location: Tourist walkways, Near bridges, Pedestrian areas

scams.name: Friendship Bracelet Scam
scams.description: A vendor approaches and grabs your hand, quickly weaving a colorful friendship bracelet around your wrist. Once tied on with a difficult knot, they demand payment of 10-20 euros. If you refuse, they become aggressive or an accomplice uses the distraction to pickpocket you.
scams.avoidance: Keep your hands in your pockets when approached. Say 'Non' firmly and keep walking. Don't let anyone touch you or attach anything.
scams.location: Tourist attractions, Near churches, Pedestrian areas

scams.name: Rose/Flower Scam
scams.description: A seller approaches couples dining outdoors, offering a rose with 'Flower for the pretty lady!' The moment you touch or accept the flower, they demand 5-10 euros. If you try to return it, they refuse and become aggressive until you pay out of embarrassment.
scams.avoidance: Don't touch or accept any flowers offered. A simple 'Non, merci' and wave sends them away. Ask restaurant staff to intervene if needed.
scams.location: Restaurant terraces, Romantic spots, Evening entertainment areas

scams.name: Fake Police Scam
scams.description: Criminals pose as police officers, quickly flashing fake badges. They claim they need to check your wallet for counterfeit bills or 'drug money.' While examining your wallet, they steal cash. Sometimes a 'tourist' accomplice first asks you to break a large bill, then the fake officer arrives.
scams.avoidance: Know that real police never ask to see your wallet - only ID documents. Suggest going to the nearest police station to verify their identity. Call 17 if unsure.
scams.location: Metro stations, Tourist areas, Near bars at night

scams.name: Taxi Overcharging
scams.description: Unscrupulous taxi drivers target tourists unfamiliar with Lyon's layout. They may take long routes to inflate the fare, 'forget' to start the meter, or select the higher night/weekend rate during regular hours. Airport runs are particularly vulnerable - the fare from Lyon-Saint Exupéry to the city center should be around €50-70.
scams.avoidance: Only use taxis from official ranks. Ensure the meter is zeroed before departure. Use GPS on your phone to follow the route. Consider using Uber or Bolt.
scams.location: Lyon-Saint Exupéry Airport, Part-Dieu station, Perrache station, Outside nightclubs

scams.name: ATM Skimming / Private ATM Scam
scams.description: Criminals attach skimming devices to ATMs that steal your card data and PIN. Private ATM companies like Euronet place machines that charge excessive fees and poor exchange rates - up to 4x more than bank ATMs. They may offer Dynamic Currency Conversion at terrible rates.
scams.avoidance: Use ATMs inside bank branches only. Look for major French banks: BNP Paribas, Société Générale, LCL. Always cover keypad when entering PIN. Decline dynamic currency conversion.
scams.location: Private ATMs in tourist areas, ATMs on busy streets, Near train stations

scams.name: Broken Camera Scam
scams.description: Someone asks you to take their photo using their camera. After you return the camera, they claim you broke it and demand money for repairs. The 'camera' was already broken - they use it repeatedly for this scam.
scams.avoidance: Politely decline to take photos with others' cameras. If accused of damage, suggest filing a police report together - scammers will refuse.
scams.location: Tourist attractions, Photo-worthy spots

scams.name: Friendship Bracelet/String Scam
scams.description: Someone approaches you in a friendly manner and loops a coloured string or bracelet around your wrist before you can refuse. Once it's tied on, they claim it's a 'gift' and then aggressively demand cash payment, typically 5-20 euros. They may physically grab your wrist to tie the bracelet, making it difficult to refuse. The scammer creates social pressure by making a scene if you try to walk away without paying.
scams.avoidance: Keep your hands in your pockets when walking through tourist areas. Say 'Non, merci' firmly and keep walking. Do not stop to engage in conversation. If they grab your wrist, firmly remove their hand and walk away.
scams.location: Old Port (Vieux-Port), La Canebière, Tourist areas

scams.name: Gold Ring Scam
scams.description: A passer-by 'finds' a gold ring on the ground near you and picks it up, showing it to you and claiming it's yours or that you must have dropped it. When you say it's not yours, they offer to let you have it as it 'must be your lucky day.' They then ask for a reward or 'finder's fee' for their 'honesty.' The ring is actually cheap brass or gold-plated and worthless, worth perhaps a few cents.
scams.avoidance: Ignore anyone who approaches claiming to have found something valuable. Say 'Non, ce n'est pas à moi' (No, it's not mine) and walk away. Never accept items from strangers. Do not engage in conversation about found items.
scams.location: Old Port (Vieux-Port), La Canebière, Near train stations, Tourist walkways

scams.name: Pickpocketing
scams.description: Marseille has significant pickpocketing issues, especially in tourist areas. Thieves often work in groups using distraction techniques. Common methods include: children swarming tourists near the train station while accomplices steal valuables; someone asking for directions while another person lifts your wallet; creating a commotion or 'accidentally' bumping into you; standing unusually close on the metro, especially when doors open and close (thieves grab items and step off quickly). The area around Gare Saint-Charles has a particularly heavy concentration of pickpockets.
scams.avoidance: Wear a cross-body bag in front, not behind. Keep phones out of back pockets. Never sling a bag over a chair back at outdoor tables. Use a money belt for large amounts of cash and cards. Be extra vigilant when metro doors open and close. Avoid displaying expensive watches, cameras, or jewelry. Keep only what you need for the day; leave valuables in hotel safe.
scams.location: Vieux-Port (Old Port), Gare Saint-Charles train station, Metro Line 1, La Canebière, Crowded markets, Beach shuttles to Calanques, Old Port tourist trains

scams.name: Fake Charity Petition Scam
scams.description: A person approaches with a clipboard, often claiming to be deaf-mute, and asks if you speak English. They then request you sign a 'petition' for a charity, supposedly supporting deaf or disabled people. The petition is in English (a red flag in France) and looks official. After signing, they demand a donation, pointing to text on the paper claiming you agreed to donate when you signed. While you're distracted signing, an accomplice may be going through your pockets or bag. Even if there's no accomplice, you may feel pressured into giving money for a fake cause.
scams.avoidance: Never stop for clipboard petitioners. Say 'Non' firmly and keep walking. Never sign anything on the street. Keep hands in pockets and maintain distance. If approached, check that your belongings are secure immediately.
scams.location: Vieux-Port, Near tourist attractions, Gare Saint-Charles, La Canebière

scams.name: Three Card Monte / Shell Game
scams.description: You encounter a group gathered around someone playing a simple card game (find the queen) or shell game (find the ball under the cup). The game looks easy to win, and you watch people (who are actually accomplices called 'shills') winning money easily. When you try to play, you lose every time because the operator uses sleight of hand to cheat. The game depends on a lookout watching for police, a 'roper' to bring in players, and shills who pretend to win. The moment you put down money, it's gone. Some operations may become aggressive if you try to leave without paying.
scams.avoidance: Never play street gambling games - they are always rigged. Do not stop to watch. Remember that bystanders are likely accomplices. The shell game is fraud in France.
scams.location: Busy tourist areas, Near the Old Port, Public squares, Near train stations

scams.name: Taxi Overcharging / Unlicensed Taxi Scam
scams.description: Unlicensed taxi drivers or unscrupulous licensed drivers target tourists arriving at the airport or train station. They may refuse to use the meter, quote a fixed price that's significantly inflated, take unnecessarily long routes, or claim the meter is broken. Some unlicensed operators solicit fares inside terminals. At night, prices can be quoted at 2-3x the normal rate. Official airport-to-city fare should be approximately 50 euros daytime and 60 euros at night.
scams.avoidance: Use only official taxis from designated ranks (outside Arrivals Hall at airport). Confirm the fare before getting in. Insist on the meter being used. Know the approximate fare in advance (50€ day/60€ night airport to center). Use ride-sharing apps like Uber for transparent pricing. Note driver ID and license plate if overcharged - report to police.
scams.location: Marseille Provence Airport, Gare Saint-Charles train station, Outside nightlife areas late at night

scams.name: Restaurant Overcharging
scams.description: Some restaurants in tourist areas use various tactics to overcharge visitors. Common schemes include: showing a menu with reasonable prices but charging more on the bill; offering 'specials' verbally that turn out to be extremely expensive; adding items to the bill that weren't ordered; automatically serving expensive bottled water instead of free tap water when you ask for water; insisting tourists must tip when service is already included in France; offering only medium or large size drinks at inflated prices; giving tourists a different (higher priced) menu than locals. One documented case showed a Marseille restaurant advertising a 28€ menu where 9 of 13 dishes required an additional 5-10€ each.
scams.avoidance: Ask for the French menu and compare prices. Request 'une carafe d'eau' (pitcher of tap water) - it's free. Verify prices for specials before ordering. Review the bill carefully ('l'addition') against what you ordered. Tipping is not required in France - service is included. Choose restaurants away from main tourist thoroughfares. Read recent online reviews.
scams.location: Restaurants around Vieux-Port, Heavily touristed areas, Restaurants with picture menus outside

scams.name: ATM Skimming / Card Trap Scam
scams.description: Criminals install skimming devices on ATMs that capture your card data and PIN. This can include: an overlay placed over the card slot that records magnetic stripe data; a fake keypad overlay or hidden camera recording your PIN entry; or a device that traps your card inside the machine. In the card trap version, your card gets stuck and a 'helpful' stranger appears offering advice, watching as you enter your PIN multiple times. Once you leave to seek help, they retrieve your card and use it with the PIN they observed.
scams.avoidance: Use ATMs inside banks during business hours. Cover the keypad with your hand when entering PIN. Check for loose or unusual parts before inserting card. If card gets stuck, do not leave - call your bank immediately. Never accept help from strangers at ATMs. Enable transaction alerts on your bank account. Avoid standalone ATMs in tourist areas.
scams.location: Standalone ATMs in tourist areas, ATMs in dimly lit areas, Non-bank ATMs

scams.name: Fake Police Scam
scams.description: Two people in official-looking uniforms or plain clothes approach you, flash fake badges quickly, and claim to be 'Tourist Police' or plainclothes officers. They claim they need to check your wallet for counterfeit bills, 'drug money,' or verify your identity. While examining your wallet, they discreetly remove bills. They may also ask to see your passport and credit cards. By the time you realize money is missing, they've disappeared. Some variations involve accusing you of a minor infraction and demanding an immediate 'fine' paid in cash.
scams.avoidance: Real French police never check tourists' wallets on the street. Ask to see ID clearly and note badge number. Insist on going to the nearest police station before handing anything over. Never give your wallet to anyone on the street regardless of uniform. Call 17 (police) if suspicious.
scams.location: Streets near tourist areas, Public transportation, Near bars at night

scams.name: Bump and Spill Distraction Theft
scams.description: A well-dressed person 'accidentally' spills something (coffee, ice cream, sauce) on your clothing. They apologize profusely and begin helping to wipe off the stain, using the commotion to distract you while an accomplice steals your wallet, phone, or bag. Alternatively, a jogger may bump into you hard, knocking you off balance. While helping you recover, they or a partner steal your belongings. Another variation involves someone dropping coins or papers near you - as you helpfully bend down to assist, an accomplice grabs your bag from behind.
scams.avoidance: Immediately check your belongings if anyone spills on or bumps you. Do not let strangers touch your clothing. Step back from anyone getting too close. Keep bags secured and in front of you. Be suspicious of any unusual contact in crowded areas.
scams.location: Metro stations, Crowded tourist areas, Outside cafes and restaurants

scams.name: Rental Car Break-in / Smash and Grab
scams.description: Marseille and the surrounding Provence region are notorious for car break-ins targeting tourists, especially at beaches and the Calanques. Thieves identify rental cars by license plates, sterile interiors, and window stickers. They smash windows and steal bags in seconds, even if you're only away for a few minutes. Some thieves target cars in traffic - approaching at red lights or in slow traffic to grab items through open windows. One traveler reported their car was completely stripped of belongings after parking near a beach for just 10 minutes.
scams.avoidance: Never leave anything visible in the car - even empty bags look promising to thieves. Remove all rental car identifying stickers if possible. Park in attended lots when available. Never park near the Calanques trailheads with valuables in car. Take all valuables with you. Keep windows closed and doors locked even in traffic. Use the trunk for storage, but load it before arriving at destination.
scams.location: Calanques parking areas, Beach parking lots, Roadside stops, Scenic viewpoints

scams.name: Vacation Rental / Airbnb Scam
scams.description: Scammers create fake vacation rental listings on platforms like Airbnb or independent websites, using stolen photos from legitimate properties. The listing shows an attractive apartment at below-market prices. Victims pay deposits or full rental fees, then arrive to find the property doesn't exist, belongs to someone else, or is drastically different from the listing. In the 'bait and switch' version, the host cancels just before check-in, claiming the original property is unavailable, and offers an inferior substitute. France, including Paris and coastal areas near Marseille, has seen an epidemic of such scams.
scams.avoidance: Book only through established platforms with buyer protection. Never pay outside the platform. Read reviews carefully and check host history. Reverse image search listing photos. If price seems too good to be true, it probably is. Verify the address exists on Google Maps/Street View. Contact host with specific questions about the property.
scams.location: Online - before arrival

scams.name: Beach Theft at Prado Beaches
scams.description: While tourists swim or relax with their attention elsewhere, thieves steal unattended belongings from beach towels and bags. The Prado beaches are pleasant during the day but have many shaded areas that provide cover for thieves. At the Calanques, visitors often leave belongings at the beach while swimming, making easy targets. Some thieves work in pairs - one distracts with conversation while the other takes items from nearby spots.
scams.avoidance: Never leave valuables unattended on the beach. Use a waterproof pouch for phone and money while swimming. Take turns watching belongings with travel companions. Leave valuables at your accommodation. Avoid beaches late at night, especially alone. Use beach lockers where available.
scams.location: Prado beaches, Urban beaches, Calanques swimming areas

scams.name: La Mere Poulard Restaurant Price Trap
scams.description: The famous La Mere Poulard restaurants charge extreme prices for their signature souffle omelettes, banking on century-old hype rather than quality. Visitors report paying 40-80 euros for a basic omelette that is often dry, flavorless, and 'nothing extraordinary.' A bottle of cider costs 19-26 euros here versus under 3 euros at supermarkets. Service is notoriously poor with 30-40 minute waits to even have orders taken.
scams.avoidance: Skip dining on the island entirely. If you must eat on-island, check menu prices carefully before sitting. Eat at restaurants in nearby Pontorson or Cancale instead. Bring a picnic lunch to the island.
scams.location: La Mere Poulard restaurant, L'Auberge de La Mere Poulard, La Mere Poulard Cafe, Grande Rue

scams.name: Island Restaurant Tourist Trap
